messages:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up proposal: compress console->query surface into a compact intent facade + auth preflight. goals: smaller per-request payloads, earlier RBAC, cheaper canaries. thoughts?

alex: sounds promising. can you sketch the new request flow? specifically how panel-level perms and projection logic are handled. :thinking: 

maya: high level runbook: 1) console emits a small intent proto (route id, projection set, tenant id, client hints) instead of the full client graph 2) query-facade does auth preflight + lightweight routing 3) facade expands to engine calls only for permitted fields 4) legacy full-graph path kept as escape hatch.

kevin: proto size vs current payload? worried about serialization CPU vs network savings.

maya: benches: current full client graph ~1.8KB avg, intent proto ~230B. parse time at facade edge drops ~10-15ms, also gives cheaper cache keys.

zoe: RBAC note: pushing checks earlier demands a canonical projection grammar. otherwise policies become brittle and may under/over-share. we should define a minimal projection DSL.

alex: agreed. but panels that rely on dynamic post-aggregation filters are tricky. can we support a tiny filter DSL in the intent?

maya: yes, small DSL for route-level projections & filters only. heavy queries use legacy /query (tagged heavy) routed to a dedicated pool with stricter SLOs and audit.

kevin: rollout strategy? avoid big cutovers. proposal: 1) deploy facade behind feature flag 2) route 5% traffic to facade with shadowing to legacy 3) enable strict auth-preflight only on canary 4) monitor ER and latency.

zoe: metrics to add: auth_mismatch_count, facade_expansion_failures, percent_heavy_queries, p50/p95 end-to-end latency by route, intent_cache_hit_ratio. also add audit_log for legacy-escape cases.

alex: contract/versioning: how do frontends fall back if facade doesn't understand newer intent?

maya: include X-Intent-Version header. fallback: 412 -> console retries legacy path. keep 2 versions active for ~3 months.

kevin: infra ops: extra instances at edge but each is light CPU. consider colocating with gateway to reuse TLS and rate limits. autoscale for short CPU spikes.

zoe: security: preflight must call central policy engine (OPA) with normalized projection. watch amplification where many small intents flood OPA. consider batching OPA checks per-tenant or route.

alex: +1 batching; also add small LRU cache for allow results keyed by (tenant,route,projection-hash) with a short TTL (~30s).

maya: caching OK; invalidate on role-change webhook. will add a role-change binding.

kevin: migration checklist sketch: 1) implement facade behind flag 2) shadow expansions for canary traffic 3) enable preflight on read-only routes first 4) expand to interactive dashboards 5) route legacy-heavy panels to special pool.

maya: example intent payload I'll include in the RFC: ```
{
  "intent_v":"1",
  "route":"dashboard_tile.v2",
  "tenant":"t-42",
  "projection":["user.name","usage.agg30"],
  "hints":{"max_rows":100,"prefetch":true}
}
```

zoe: also include mapping table legacy-node -> projection-term so expansion is deterministic. add compatibility tests that diff legacy vs facade-expanded outputs for sample panels.

infra-bot: CI: integration-tests/console-facade failed on staging (auth-suite). https://ci.redwood.internal/12345 :warning:

kevin: thanks infra-bot. maya, failing test is probably role-change invalidation. add webhook binding to test harness.

maya: will push patch with webhook + LRU tweak. plan to post RFC this afternoon for async review. :thumbsup:
